No code, no templates to wrestle with, live on a public URL in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "build a personal website with AI", "category": "Use-Cases", "bodyHtml": "

A personal website is one of the few internet assets that is entirely yours: not a profile on someone else's platform, not a link in a bio, but a page that says who you are on your own terms. The problem has never been the idea — it's the setup. Picking a page builder, wrestling with templates, figuring out hosting. AI removes that entire layer. You describe the site you want, and it gets built. Here's how to do it properly.

What a good personal website actually needs

Before you write a prompt, it helps to know what you're asking for. Almost every effective personal site, regardless of profession, comes down to four things:

  • A clear intro or bio — who you are, in a sentence or two, not a resume dump.
  • What you do or care about — your work, your focus, your interests, stated plainly.
  • A way to reach you — email, a contact form, or a link to a platform where you're reachable.
  • Links to your other work or profiles — portfolio pieces, social profiles, writing, projects, GitHub, whatever proves the bio.

Everything else — a photo grid, a blog section, a testimonials block — is optional polish on top of those four essentials. Keep that list in mind and your prompt will write itself.

The one-prompt approach

The fastest way to get a personal site live is to describe it once, completely, in a single message. Instead of typing something vague like make me a personal website, include the sections you actually want, your name, your field, and the tone. The more specific the prompt, the less back-and-forth you'll need afterward. Vague prompts produce generic sites; specific prompts produce sites that already look like a first draft worth publishing.

A real example prompt

Here's a prompt you could copy, paste, and adjust for yourself right now:

Build a personal website for me, a freelance UX designer named Mara Chen. I want a clean, minimal, dark-themed homepage with a short intro section that says who I am and what I do, a section listing three areas I specialize in (mobile app design, design systems, and user research), a projects section with three placeholder project cards I can edit later, and a contact section with my email address and links to my Dribbble and LinkedIn profiles. Keep the layout simple with plenty of whitespace and one accent color.

That single prompt gives Kodely everything it needs: your identity, your focus areas, the sections you want, and a visual direction. You'll get a working site back in one pass, not a blank template you still have to fill in.

What Kodely actually generates

This is the part that separates a real AI website builder from a form-filling wizard. When you submit a prompt, Kodely does not spit out a static HTML mockup or a locked template with your name swapped in. It generates a real Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS application — actual component files, built on a hand-crafted foundation of UI primitives so the result looks considered rather than generic. You can open the code view inside the app and read the real source files it produced, section by section, exactly as they were built.

As the app is generated, you watch a live preview render the actual compiled site in real time, not a static screenshot standing in for the real thing.

Customizing your site through chat

Once the first version exists, refining it works the same way you started: you describe the change in chat, and Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes. Want the accent color changed from blue to a warm amber? Say so. Want the projects section to hold four cards instead of three, or the bio rewritten with a different tone? Describe it in a sentence and it updates the actual code, not a copy.

Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint automatically, so if a change takes the site somewhere you don't like, rolling back to the previous version costs nothing and takes one click. That means you can experiment freely — try a bolder layout, a different section order, a new headline — without any risk of losing a version you liked better.

Publishing to a live URL

When the site looks right, publishing is a single click. Kodely puts it live at a public address on the kodely.site domain — something like marachen.kodely.site — and there's no separate hosting step, no server to configure, and no extra cost involved. Before anything goes live, Kodely scans the build for accidentally exposed secrets or API keys, so you're not shipping something you'll regret. From prompt to a real, shareable link, the whole process typically takes minutes.

FAQ

Do I need any coding experience to build a personal website with AI?

No. You describe what you want in plain English and Kodely writes the actual React components. If you're curious, you can view the generated source code inside the app, but you never have to touch it.

Can I use my own domain name?

Right now, published sites live on a free kodely.site subdomain. There's no custom domain support yet, which keeps the whole process, from prompt to live URL, completely free and instant.

Can I download the code and host it myself?

Not currently. You can view and copy your source files from within the app's code view, but there's no full-project export or zip download yet.

What if I want to edit a specific section instead of the whole page?

Just describe the section and the change you want in chat — for example, update the contact section to add my Twitter link. Kodely edits that part of the real code directly.

How much does it cost?

Signing up gives you 750 credits free, no card required, which is enough to build and publish a straightforward personal site. If you need more, top-ups start at nine dollars for five hundred credits, and credits never expire. A build that fails to compile is never charged.

Will my site look like a template?

No two prompts generate the same layout, and because Kodely builds from real components rather than filling in a fixed template, the more specific your prompt, the more distinct the result.

Your bio, your work, your links, live on the internet in the time it takes to describe them. Build your personal website free and see your first version in minutes.
